title: The Turning of the Face and the Light of the Soul
english: For they depart from those things which are not contained by them. And the rights and statutes must be spoken of which have been legislated according to equality and justice, such as 'If a Hebrew acquires a child' (Deut 21:15), and the following. For all these things, the judgments are arranged as side-notes, and the following.

The judgments, being named with the rights, can signify the tested and examined words of God; for they are not called judgments because they are not being checked or being overturned. In this way even the thoughts of the righteous are judgments, that is, having been accurately examined and tested, and being this very thing similar to a rule.

Perhaps those who, not through God but through glory or something else, find fault and [call] something unblemished, are unblemished indeed, but not with God; but those who have embraced the good through God and not for the sake of anything else, are unblemished with God; for this union toward God preserves one unblemished and good. But those being uncoupled and separated from God become immediately unblemished [children], unblemished children becoming through the act of sinning.

He who has accomplished all the aforementioned things, how does he speak of his own lawlessness? It is to say that he does not wish to understand at any time; this is it: 'The mind of man leans toward evil things with care from youth' (Gen 8:21), as it flows toward sin, being enticed by pleasure. He who has given himself to the law of God protects himself from the lawlessness that overshadows men.

Perhaps also that which is called among us the mindset of the flesh, which is enmity toward God and does not submit to His law, is the lawlessness of man, from which one preserves the deeds of the body of death in the spirit and abstains from the works of the flesh. There he calls righteousness here, that which is established from the faith of Jesus Christ. For the righteousness of God has been revealed to all who believe (Rom 3:22); for to the one believing rightly, 'the faith is reckoned as righteousness' (Rom 4:3/5). And together with purity...

For you say the works of faith, which operate brightly and without stain, without which faith is dead (Ps 17:26–28). Regarding the change of face in Psalm 17:26–28, someone says these upcoming verses are to be spoken toward God, because he does not say to another, 'That you will save a humble people and humble the eyes of the proud,' but to God. Another will say that these are not spoken toward God but toward a man: that the one spending time with the holy should imitate their virtue, and the one spending time with the wicked should undergo perversion, as the divine writing of Proverbs says: 'He who walks with the wise will be wise, but he who walks with fools will be destroyed' (Prov 13:20). The interpretations are thus: 'With the holy man, O Lord, he shall be made holy,' providing him the holiness supplied from you so that, having been perfected according to it, you may bring him into the fitting promise, and the others following the one before it. He also says, 'You will pervert,' for it is possible to say, 'He perverts with a crookedness'; this is not said, but 'You will pervert.' For God perverts the one running toward evil things, blocking his way with stumbling blocks and rebuilding his paths; for to be prevented from evils is the beginning of blessing. But he who wishes to be taken toward a man says that the one associating with a holy man becomes holy from the holy things being done, as Elisha with Elijah and Timothy with Paul; and the one hastening with the innocent, having seized that one's virtue, will be innocent. Likewise, the one spending time with an elect man, but the one associating with the crooked, desiring to become like him, will pervert his own life. And he, having clarified the verses thus, turns his face toward God from 'That you will save a humble people.'
Regarding the receptive part of the soul's light, the power—that is, the mind, which some call the reasoning faculty—it is said to be its lamp, not being itself...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
